newsitem.title: POLAND: Rafako to seek strategic investor.
newsitem.headline: Rafako to seek strategic investor.

text.p: Polish industrial boilermaker Rafako SA will seek a strategic investor, foreign or domestic, from the sector to strengthen the firm's market position, the company's director said on Wednesday.
Maciej Kaczorowski told Reuters London-based Salomon Brothers would be the company's financial adviser in seeking the investor, which might be offered the company's new shares.

"Salomon Brothers will ask on our behalf the domestic and foreign firms from the sector to take part in negotiations ... It is possible that the purchase of the stake will take a form of raising of the share capital," he said.
He said the stake to be sold would depended on negotiations with a prospective investor.
Kaczorowski said it was possible the investor could take between 3.17 and 4.17 million shares, approved for trade by the Polish Securities Commission in February last year.

The issue was delayed because Rafako was not satisfied with issue price of 14 zlotys, set through a book-building. The book-building was carried out after the firm showed a net loss of 56.5 million zlotys in an audited 1995 report.
Currently Rafako has 9.3 million shares outstanding.
Kaczorowski said there were several firms interested in taking the stake in Rafako, but declined to name the firms involved.

He said Rafako hoped the investor would take the stake by the end of the year. "In the first quarter we will know with whom we are going to negotiate further, but we would like to finalise it this year," Kaczorowski said.
Rafako's main shareholder is the Polish company Rafako Sp z o.o., which has 47.5 percent of shares in the firm.
